correctness.rationale: The polynomial identity follows by partitioning each permutation according to its two distinct first-column and second-column rows. Specialization B=all ones gives A=(n-2)!(J-I) of nonzero determinant, proving that the substitution w=A(B)v has an inverse on the principal open. This proves equality of schemes with the hypersurface sum(u_i*w_i)=0; its Jacobian ideal consists of every u_i and w_i and is reduced. Consequently the linear subspace is an entire local singular component. The transverse Hessian is [[0,A],[A,0]] with determinant (-1)^n(det A)^2, and the complementary-matrix degeneration divisor has degree n(n-2). An exact checker confirms 42 specializations and 6 determinant examples; finite checks do not replace the proof. The full Hessian rank-drop determinantal divisor is the double of the complementary-matrix divisor, not the divisor itself.

originality.rationale: Alper--Bogart--Velasco 2015 Remark 1.5 has the already-known singular containment and ambient codimension upper bound, but not the local ring or complementary-matrix determinant. Boralevi--Carlini--Michałek--Ventura 2024 Section 4.5 proves lower codimension bounds and states conjectures concerning global components, not the explicit full-neighborhood product or Jacobian scheme. Laubenbacher--Swanson 1998 treats ideals of size-two permanents, not this uniform all-size local model. Actual semantic searches found nearby results about unrelated singular varieties and no statement implying the claimed split form; negative searches alone do not certify novelty. Risk of an equivalent unindexed specialization persists.

value.rationale: The generic singularity and component structure of large permanent hypersurfaces remains a mathematically motivated issue, as shown by the recent 2024 codimension study and its unproved global component conjectures. This all-size result establishes an actual irreducible component of codimension 2n for each row/column pair, determines its reduced Jacobian scheme on a nonempty open, identifies the entire transverse analytic/algebraic model, and locates a natural degree n(n-2) discriminant divisor. These are reusable invariants beyond a numerical toy example or the known singularity containment; the complete singular locus is not claimed.
